item.title: Code of the Future: Habr and Sber Launch a New Season of Articles on the Role of AI in Software Development
item.description:
Artificial intelligence in IT has transformed from an experimental tool into a working one: it changes roles in teams and forces a re-evaluation of established approaches. Companies are discussing less whether AI is useful in software development and more about how to best integrate it into their processes. This is perhaps the most significant industry transformation in recent years, and we want to see it through the lens of your experience. Therefore, Habr, together with Sber, is launching a new season of "Code of the Future" articles, where you can share your practical experience using AI in software development and the relationship between AI and open source. The season runs from September 11 to November 11, 2026. Below are all the details: themes, deadlines, and rules. Read on.

Original Russian article on Habr

item.title: What do mathematicians say about the impact of AI on mathematics?
item.description:
News headlines like "AI Solved a Millennium Prize Problem" are appearing more frequently. From the outside, it can be hard to assess: where is historical precedent, and where is manufactured hype? And most importantly: what does it all mean for the future of mathematics? To bring clarity to the issue, it's useful to listen to mathematicians themselves. What do they consider suitable tasks for AI, and what are human tasks? Where do they see progress, and where do they see mere hype? What is their vision of the meaning of mathematics, and how should one approach mathematics consciously in this changed world? We at Kodik don't deal with mathematics, but with an AI code editor. Nevertheless, our team includes people with classical mathematics education, and we follow the topic with interest. Therefore, we previously translated mathematicians' opinions on the refutation of a specific Erdős problem for Habr, and now we've decided to cover their view on the current situation as a whole. Of course, opinions differ, but in this article, we've tried to gather a snapshot of the mathematical community. Read more

item.title: DLP for LLMs: How to Anonymize Requests Without Breaking Employee Search
item.description:
What happens to corporate search when employee names need to be hidden from an external LLM? Simple replacement of surnames with random markers protects data but breaks the connection between the query, found documents, and the model's response. In this article, we explore how to balance privacy and utility: where to store the mapping, why entity resolution is needed, how the policy engine makes decisions, and why it's crucial to check not only the input prompt but also the model's response. Read more

item.title: MFIs Issued a Loan to a Scammer: Who Should Be Responsible for the Consequences
item.description:
A Russian woman recently fell victim to fraud: about 60 microloans totaling over 2.5 million rubles were issued in her name, with only a photo of her passport being sufficient for the scammers. For over a year, she has faced calls and threats from collectors, while over twenty MFIs continue to try to recover the money from her. This incident is highly illustrative, reminding us once again how serious the threat of fraud remains and how costly it can be for an ordinary person. The scale of risk grows with the number of leaks: according to industry data, 326 databases of Russian companies' clients, containing about 1.175 billion records with user information, became publicly available in 2025 and the first half of 2026. This is twice the combined number of public leaks in Latin America, the Middle East, Africa, the Asia-Pacific region, and other CIS countries. In such conditions, it's no longer possible to assume that passport and other personal data remain known only to their owner; once in the public domain, they are highly likely to become a tool for scammers. Therefore, the question often becomes how quickly criminals will attempt to use them to obtain loans. In this context, another equally important question arises: who should bear responsibility for the consequences of such fraud? Let's explore the role of banks and MFIs in preventing such schemes and why reliable borrower identity verification must be a mandatory part of the loan issuance process. Read more

item.title: What it means to deploy an LLM locally: two days with vLLM, DGX Spark, and real limitations
item.description:
When I was once asked what inference is and what local model deployment looks like, I answered correctly but too generally. A few days later, I had to go through this entire process: setting up two LLMs on NVIDIA DGX Spark, a separate ASR model on AMD GPU, and connecting everything to a multi-agent platform. The article provides an engineering breakdown of why model files are not yet a service, how long context competes with KV cache and parallelism, why tokens/sec doesn't describe user latency, and why sometimes a faster model is rolled back due to quality. Read more

item.title: AI is Shifting the Center of Gravity in Development
item.description:
In the AI era, code becomes cheaper, and a quality engineering solution becomes more valuable. Therefore, it's more important not just to be able to write code quickly, but to be able to design a system so that humans and agents equally understand: what needs to be changed, why, where the boundaries lie, and what the result should be. Viaduct helps transform architectural design into a structured, verifiable context accessible to AI agents – from the system model to a Change Set that can be used to safely implement the change. Read more

item.title: I decided to check if everyone is really looking for AI engineers. Spoiler: 84% of vacancies are silent about AI
item.description:
I decided to check how many people with AI skills are currently in demand on the market. Everyone feels like AI is everywhere, indispensable, every other post in the feed is about agents. But what about the job market? I scraped hh.ru (with the help of LLM), all active vacancies in 25 categories of the "Information Technology" section in Russia - it turned out to be 34,053. Then I counted how many of them mention language models and related things: LLM, GPT, RAG, agents, prompts, Cursor, LangChain, GigaChat, and a couple of dozen other terms. Separately, how many I analyzed by the full text of the description: 853 vacancies. Find out the truth

item.title: How 17B Active Parameters Beat 70B Dense: The Anatomy of Mixture-of-Experts (MoE)
item.description:
If you blinked and missed the moment when neural network developers stopped bragging about the sheer number of parameters and started flexing about modest active parameter counts, this article is for you. Today, I'll explain how open-source flagships suddenly became MoE, why Qwen3.5 with 397 billion parameters generates tokens as if it were 17B, and why no one went bankrupt buying GPUs. For those who just want to know, we'll reveal which 'office' the medical expert resides in. Read on.

item.title: Welcome to the AGI Era (According to OpenAI's Marketing Department)
item.description:
The phrase "Welcome to the AGI ERA" wasn't from Altman's tweet, but from a closed-door briefing. The press conflated two different statements into a corporate announcement that never happened. I've reconstructed the timeline, cross-referenced key figures with independent benchmark administrators, and tested the model against seven verifiable criteria: Astra passes the critic's criteria but fails the claimant's. Welcome to the breakdown.

item.title: Why Seedance 2.5 and Hailuo H3 Ignore Prompts and How to Fix It with a 3D Scene
item.description:
Hi Habr! I'm Ilya Trikhoz, co-founder and developer at GPTunneL. Today, I'll tell you about something we created when we got tired of watching expensive video models repeatedly invent their own direction instead of what we asked for. But now, you can assemble a video differently: 1) generate a 3D scene from primitives, set up cameras; 2) get a render reference, which Seedance 2.5 or Hailuo H3 will follow precisely. Angles, timing, cuts – everything is predictable, stays on the canvas, and any step can be redone. Instead of persuading the model with text, we show it directly (with cubes, so to speak). So, meet the "3D Scene" node in our workflow constructor. Read more
